Energean First-Half Performance Hit by Lost Israeli Volumes
Energean's first-half earnings fell after it temporarily paused Israeli production due to conflict in the Middle East, though higher oil and gas prices softened the blow.

The London-listed energy company said adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization and exploration costs dropped 5% on the same period a year prior to $478 million. Pretax profit rose to $178 million from $174 million after net foreign exchange gains and lower finance costs helped offset lost revenue.

The fall came as production from Israel declined 7% after output was paused for 41 days early in the conflict between the U.S. and Israel and Iran. Production has since returned and the company Wednesday backed its revised full-year target of 130,000 to 140,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day.
The drop in sales was partly offset by a 29% increase in realized liquids prices, the company said.
The company's dividend fell 33% to 40 cents a share from 60 cents last year.
